transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess what finally made me come in is this feeling that I’ve messed things up for everybody. Like I keep thinking I’ve ruined things, even when it’s probably stuff other people would just fix and move on from.

I’m in an apprenticeship, and lately I just feel like I’m fake being there, like I don’t actually deserve to be around people who know what they’re doing. And then I start thinking I’m letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices, which sounds kind of dramatic when I say it out loud, but it feels really real in my head. Like I’m supposed to be someone people can count on, and instead I’m just… disappointing everyone. That’s mostly why I’m here.
Do you tend to avoid social situations because you’re afraid people will judge or reject you?

I don’t know if I’d put it exactly that way. I mean, I do worry what people think of me sometimes, especially at work, because everyone seems like they know what they’re doing and I’m still learning. But I don’t think I’m, like, avoiding people because I’m scared they’ll reject me.

I still go in, I still talk to people, I still try to do what I’m supposed to do. It’s more that afterward I’ll replay things and wonder if I sounded stupid or if they think I don’t belong there. But I wouldn’t say I’m staying away from social stuff specifically because of that. At least… I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah… I think it did start after a change, not like one huge dramatic thing, but when I started this sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.

That was about five months ago, I think. Before that I’d get stressed, obviously, because the apprenticeship is already a lot, but it didn’t feel like this constant pattern of questioning myself and feeling like I’m letting everyone down. Once I added the certification, it was like suddenly there was this extra layer of pressure, and I kept comparing myself to people who seemed more confident or further along.

So, yeah, I’d say this whole thing has been going on for around five months, since I began that certification program.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because “depressed” feels like a big word. I’ve definitely had days where I feel really low on myself, like I’m disappointed in myself or I can’t stop thinking I’m not measuring up. But if you mean down all day, every day, or most days in a really clear way… I don’t know that I’ve been tracking it like that.

It’s more like it comes in waves, especially when I start thinking about work or the certification or whether people are noticing I’m behind. Then I can get pretty stuck in it. But I don’t know if I’d say I’m depressed most days. Maybe stressed and kind of ashamed-feeling, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when you try to stop?

I’m not sure I’d call it “a lot of different things,” honestly. I do worry, but it feels pretty centered around certain things — mostly whether I’m doing well enough, whether I’m falling behind, or whether I handled something wrong.

Like, if I make a mistake or I think I might’ve seemed unsure, I can get stuck on that and keep going over it in my head even when I’m trying not to. But I don’t know if I’m worrying excessively about everything, like money and health and my family and random disasters or whatever. It doesn’t really feel that broad.

It’s more like once my brain latches onto a specific thing, it keeps picking at it. I can tell myself, “Okay, stop thinking about this, you already went over it,” but then I’ll still come back to it. So… yes and no, I guess. I worry more than I want to, but I’m not sure it’s about a lot of different things.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I hadn’t really called it that, but lately it’s like the stuff that normally makes me feel like me just kind of… doesn’t pull me in.

Like, I’ll walk right past my sketchbook and not even feel the usual little urge to sit down and draw something, even if I have time. And volleyball, too — I’ve skipped it a few times, and normally I’d feel disappointed missing it, or at least I’d miss seeing people and moving around, but lately it’s more like, “Eh, I guess I’m not going,” and I don’t feel much either way.

Same with the volunteer group texts. Those used to make me feel connected, like I was doing something useful outside of work and school stuff. Now I see the messages come in and I just ignore them, not even because I hate it or anything. It’s just like there’s no spark there. I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but it does feel like those things don’t hit the same right now.
Have you noticed your sleep changing lately?

Yeah, it’s changed. It’s been kind of all over the place, actually.

For a while I was getting by on, like, three or four hours of sleep and somehow still showing up for work and class feeling… not tired exactly, more like wired. Like I’d be up way too late, sleep barely at all, and then still be moving the next day like my body was running on something else. I remember thinking, “Okay, this probably isn’t great,” but also I was still functioning, so I kind of brushed it off.

But lately it’s different. Now I’ll lie down and just not be able to fall asleep, even when I know I need to. Or I do fall asleep and then wake up before my alarm, and it feels like I didn’t actually rest. Like technically I was in bed, but my brain and body don’t feel reset at all. It’s frustrating because I’ll look at the clock and start calculating how much time I have left, which obviously doesn’t help. So yes, definitely my sleep hasn’t been normal.
During that time when you were sleeping only three or four hours, did you also feel unusually energized or high?

Yeah… I think “energized” is probably the right word, but it was more than just having a good day or feeling motivated. There were stretches — like weeks — where I felt almost too good, like everything was kind of clicking and I had this feeling like Miami was mine, like I could just move through the city and handle anything.

And at first it didn’t feel like a problem, because compared to feeling tired or stuck, it honestly felt kind of amazing. I’d be sleeping three or four hours and still feel like I had this extra charge in me. Like I didn’t need as much rest as everyone else, or like slowing down was the thing that would mess me up.

But it wasn’t just happy, either. That’s the part that makes me a little uncomfortable to admit. I was also way more touchy. If a coworker made some little comment, or if someone slowed me down when I was trying to get something done, I’d snap way harder than I normally would. Like, I’d hear myself getting sharp, and part of me would be like, “Why are you reacting like that?” but in the moment it felt completely justified, like they were in my way.

So yeah, I guess I did feel unusually energized or high, but it came with this edge to it too. Like really up, but also really easy to set off.
During those stretches when you felt especially energized, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I don’t think I would’ve called it “powerful” at the time, because that sounds kind of dramatic, but looking back, that’s basically what it was.

I had this really strong feeling like I could see solutions other people just weren’t seeing. Like in class or on job sites, when instructors or the senior guys were explaining how something should be done, I’d be sitting there thinking, “Okay, but why are we doing it that way when there’s obviously a better way?” And not just, like, a normal suggestion. It was more like I genuinely thought I could design something better than them — better than people who had been doing it for years.

There was this whole idea in my head that if people would just listen to me, I could change how every building in Miami handled water. Like I was right on the edge of figuring out something huge, and everyone else was moving too slow or being stuck in old habits. At the time it felt completely clear to me, like confidence, like certainty. Now saying it out loud, it sounds… kind of much. But yeah, during those stretches, I definitely felt like I could do things other people couldn’t.
During those energized stretches, did you do things that were unusually risky or impulsive for you?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I guess it depends what you mean by risky or impulsive.

Like, if you mean something really obvious or out of character where I look back and go, “Wow, that was dangerous,” nothing specific is jumping out at me right now. I don’t have a clear example in my head the way I do with the sleep or feeling overly confident. It’s more like I can remember feeling sped up and very sure of myself, but I’m having a harder time separating whether I actually did anything risky from just feeling like I could.

I might need you to give me examples of what you mean — like spending money, driving fast, quitting something, getting into situations I normally wouldn’t — because without that, I’m kind of scanning my memory and not landing on anything definite.
During those energized stretches, did your behavior cause problems at work, school, or with other people?

Yeah… it has, and that’s probably the part I feel the most embarrassed about, honestly. Because I can explain away a lot of the internal stuff to myself, like, “Okay, I was just really motivated,” or “I had a lot of ideas,” but the work and school side is harder to ignore.

My instructors have had to come after me more than once about sketches I said I was going to finish. Like, layout sketches or planning stuff where I’d be so convinced I had this better version in my head, and then I’d start it, get pulled into another idea, revise it too much, or just not turn in what I was supposed to when I was supposed to. And then it makes me look careless, which I hate, because I’m not trying to be careless. I actually care a lot.

And with my foreman, it’s kind of similar. He’s had to chase me about things taking longer than they should, or work that’s not moving at the pace it needs to. Not because I don’t know how to do it, but because I get caught up in doing it my way or thinking through all these extra angles, and then the actual job slows down. It’s really frustrating to admit that out loud.

I’m scared, honestly, that I’m getting close to messing up the apprenticeship and the certification I worked really hard to get. Like, I don’t think everything is ruined, but I can feel that I’m pushing it. People are noticing. And that scares me, because this isn’t just a random job to me — I’ve put a lot into it, and I don’t want my behavior during those stretches to be the reason I lose ground.
How long did those energized stretches usually last?

It’s been… I’d say this whole pattern has been going on for about five months now. It wasn’t just one random week where I got fired up and then went back to normal.

It really started after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship. That’s when I noticed these stretches of feeling really energized and locked in started happening more, or at least became obvious enough that other people were reacting to it. Before that, I don’t think I would’ve described it the same way.

So, yeah — about five months altogether. The energized periods kind of come in stretches within that, but the overall pattern started around then.
When one of those energized stretches happened, did it last at least 4 days in a row?

I think so, but I’m trying not to overstate it because I didn’t exactly keep a calendar of it. The clearest thing I can say is that this whole pattern has been going on for about five months, starting after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.

Within that, the energized periods weren’t just like one good afternoon or one late night where I got excited about something. They felt like stretches, like several days where I was in that mode and it carried over from one day into the next. So yes, I’d say at least some of them lasted around four days or more, but I’m not sure I can give you exact start and stop dates.

I don’t have a clear example in my head the way I do with the sleep or feeling overly confident. It’s more like I can remember feeling sped up and very sure of myself, but I’m having a harder time separating whether I actually did anything risky from just feeling like I could.

I might need you to give me examples of what you mean — like spending money, driving fast, quitting something, getting into situations I normally wouldn’t — because without that, I’m kind of scanning my memory and not landing on anything definite.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the elevated mood/energy caused clear impairment in functioning, which helps distinguish hypomania from a full mood episode and separates bipolar disorder from adjustment disorder or major depression.
doctor.question: During those energized stretches, did your behavior cause problems at work, school, or with other people?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My instructors and foreman have had to chase me about unfinished sketches and slower work, and I’m scared I’m close to damaging the apprenticeship and certification I worked hard to get.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the energized stretches caused problems in work, school, or relationships, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it has, and that’s probably the part I feel the most embarrassed about, honestly. Because I can explain away a lot of the internal stuff to myself, like, “Okay, I was just really motivated,” or “I had a lot of ideas,” but the work and school side is harder to ignore.

My instructors have had to come after me more than once about sketches I said I was going to finish. Like, layout sketches or planning stuff where I’d be so convinced I had this better version in my head, and then I’d start it, get pulled into another idea, revise it too much, or just not turn in what I was supposed to when I was supposed to. And then it makes me look careless, which I hate, because I’m not trying to be careless. I actually care a lot.

And with my foreman, it’s kind of similar. He’s had to chase me about things taking longer than they should, or work that’s not moving at the pace it needs to. Not because I don’t know how to do it, but because I get caught up in doing it my way or thinking through all these extra angles, and then the actual job slows down. It’s really frustrating to admit that out loud.

I’m scared, honestly, that I’m getting close to messing up the apprenticeship and the certification I worked really hard to get. Like, I don’t think everything is ruined, but I can feel that I’m pushing it. People are noticing. And that scares me, because this isn’t just a random job to me — I’ve put a lot into it, and I don’t want my behavior during those stretches to be the reason I lose ground.

inference.note: Added clearer evidence for a hypomanic syndrome: decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, grandiosity, and resulting impairment at work/school, making bipolar II spectrum more likely and adjustment disorder less likely.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the energized periods lasted at least 4 days, which is key to distinguishing hypomania/bipolar II from a depressive disorder.
doctor.question: How long did those energized stretches usually last?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This whole pattern has been going on for about five months, starting after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long the energized stretches lasted, which is directly about duration.

patient.answer:
It’s been… I’d say this whole pattern has been going on for about five months now. It wasn’t just one random week where I got fired up and then went back to normal.

It really started after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship. That’s when I noticed these stretches of feeling really energized and locked in started happening more, or at least became obvious enough that other people were reacting to it. Before that, I don’t think I would’ve described it the same way.

So, yeah — about five months altogether. The energized periods kind of come in stretches within that, but the overall pattern started around then.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the energized periods lasted at least 4 days continuously, which would support hypomania over major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: When one of those energized stretches happened, did it last at least 4 days in a row?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This whole pattern has been going on for about five months, starting after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long the energized stretches lasted, specifically whether they persisted for at least 4 days in a row.

patient.answer:
I think so, but I’m trying not to overstate it because I didn’t exactly keep a calendar of it. The clearest thing I can say is that this whole pattern has been going on for about five months, starting after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.

Within that, the energized periods weren’t just like one good afternoon or one late night where I got excited about something. They felt like stretches, like several days where I was in that mode and it carried over from one day into the next. So yes, I’d say at least some of them lasted around four days or more, but I’m not sure I can give you exact start and stop dates.

inference.note: New information supports hypomanic episodes lasting at least 4 days with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, grandiosity, and functional consequences; combined with depressive symptoms/anhedonia, this narrows from bipolar disorder NOS and major depressive episode to bipolar II disorder, current or most recent episode hypomanic.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent distinct stretches over the past 5 months of elevated/irritable mood and increased energy with decreased need for sleep, grandiose/confident thinking, and work/school impairment lasting at least about 4 days, consistent with a hypomanic episode. There are also depressive symptoms (guilt, anhedonia, insomnia, low mood waves), supporting bipolar affective disorder, current episode hypomanic. Adjustment disorder and mild depressive episode were considered because symptoms began after a psychosocial stressor and include self-doubt and low mood, but the clear hypomanic syndrome is more specific and better explains the presentation.
